mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months compresses equity discount rates, producing statistically significant positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate accommodative policy.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns do not exhibit a statistically significant positive correlation with prior 3-month FEDFUNDS declines (Rank IC < 0.03 or t-test p > 0.05 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0% in a 3-month period, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger equity sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals contraction in consumer demand, triggering negative equity returns as recessionary fears dominate the market over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in GDPC1 and HOUST does not produce negative 20-day returns in > 60% of cases, or the interaction Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When manufacturing production (INDPRO) falls below 90.0, it indicates supply chain disruption that reduces corporate earnings growth, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances when INDPRO < 90.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP growth (GDPC1) over the prior 6 months signals expanding economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings accelerate.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns do not exhibit a statistically significant positive correlation with prior 6-month GDP growth (Rank IC < 0.03 or t-test p > 0.05 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% in a 3-month period, it indicates monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in > 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) signals labor market tightness that accelerates wage inflation, triggering negative equity returns as central banks tighten policy over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in PAYEMS and decrease in UNRATE does not produce negative 20-day returns in > 60% of cases, or the interaction Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle labor market conditions (UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly), inflationary pressures trigger monetary tightening that produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances when late-cycle labor conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.
